frame_account_level.granularity: ACCOUNT-LEVEL — same across every move (gap: not per-move yet)

frame_permove.granularity: move-level (per-move frame reader; veers measured vs account baseline)

moves.label: M1
moves.paraphrase: Once the rest-day had ended, the three named women purchased aromatic spices intending to go and dress the body.
moves.agent: Mary Magdalene, Mary mother of James, and Salome
moves.outcome: spices in hand, with the intent to come and anoint him
moves.sitz: post-burial preparation practice among Jewish women following a sabbath-halted death
moves.paradigm: corpse-care / anointing of the dead
moves.narrator: anonymous third-person teller relating the women's actions

moves.label: M2
moves.paraphrase: At daybreak on the week's first day they arrived at the burial place.
moves.outcome: their arrival at the tomb at sunrise
moves.sitz: early-morning travel to a rock-cut tomb outside the city
moves.paradigm: pilgrimage to a gravesite for mourning-rites
moves.narrator: same third-person teller, marking time and place

moves.label: M3
moves.paraphrase: As they walked they were voicing a worry to one another.
moves.outcome: the question uttered aloud among them
moves.sitz: small group in transit, aware of the sealed tomb they are about to reach
moves.paradigm: practical anticipation of an obstacle to the anointing
moves.narrator: third-person teller reporting the women's own speech

moves.label: M4
moves.paraphrase: They ask who will move the sealing-stone aside for them.
moves.substrate: the stone at the tomb's door
moves.outcome: not-stated (open question, no answerer named)
moves.sitz: women physically incapable of shifting a large sealing-stone alone
moves.paradigm: practical problem of gaining access to a sealed grave
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting their internal deliberation

moves.label: M5
moves.paraphrase: Aside from the narrator: the stone was of great size.
moves.outcome: not-stated
moves.sitz: teller flagging a physical fact readers need to feel the surprise of v.4b
moves.paradigm: physical description of tomb architecture
moves.narrator: third-person teller in editorial aside, warranting the women's worry

moves.label: M6
moves.paraphrase: Raising their eyes, they perceived that the stone had already been shifted aside.
moves.operation: see (that the stone was rolled back)
moves.outcome: their perception that the stone is already moved
moves.sitz: arrival at a tomb they expected to find sealed
moves.paradigm: perception-as-discovery of an unexpected state
moves.narrator: third-person teller reporting what the women visually apprehend

moves.label: M7
moves.paraphrase: The stone had already been moved back from the opening.
moves.outcome: the opening now unblocked
moves.sitz: post-hoc discovery; the doer of the rolling is precisely what the text leaves open
moves.paradigm: passive-divine / unnamed-agent state at a burial site
moves.narrator: third-person teller, reporting the perceived state (agent of the rolling unspecified)

moves.label: M8
moves.paraphrase: Once inside the tomb, they saw a young figure seated to the right in a white robe.
moves.operation: see (a young man sitting on the right, dressed in white)
moves.substrate: M6a (the young man and his posture/attire)
moves.outcome: their perception of an unexpected occupant
moves.sitz: entering a rock-cut tomb expecting a corpse and finding an unexpected living occupant
moves.paradigm: encounter with a numinous/mediating figure at a threshold
moves.narrator: third-person teller reporting the women's discovery inside the tomb

moves.label: M9
moves.paraphrase: A young figure was seated on the right side, wearing a white robe.
moves.operation: sit (dressed in white, on the right)
moves.agent: not-stated (the young man is a topic, not a doer here)
moves.outcome: not-stated
moves.sitz: the interior of the sealed tomb, occupied by a figure who should not be there
moves.paradigm: white-clad seated messenger at a right-hand position — signaling status without naming it
moves.narrator: third-person teller inside the women's perception

moves.label: M10
moves.paraphrase: They were struck with astonishment.
moves.agent: not-stated (they undergo it, not perform it)
moves.outcome: amazement as their state
moves.sitz: reaction of ordinary mourners confronted with an inexplicable scene
moves.paradigm: human awe/fear in the presence of a numinous figure
moves.narrator: third-person teller reporting the women's reaction

moves.label: M11
moves.paraphrase: The young figure addressed them.
moves.outcome: his utterance directed at the women
moves.sitz: unnamed occupant of the tomb takes the initiative to speak to the frightened women
moves.paradigm: messenger-announcement inside a sacred/liminal space
moves.narrator: third-person teller reporting the young man's speech

moves.label: M12
moves.paraphrase: He orders them to stop being astonished.
moves.outcome: an imperative to release the fear
moves.sitz: immediate pastoral response to the women's fright
moves.paradigm: 'fear not' opening of a messenger-oracle
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the young man

moves.label: M13
moves.paraphrase: He names whom they are looking for: the crucified Jesus of Nazareth.
moves.operation: identify (whom you seek: Jesus the Nazarene, the crucified one)
moves.outcome: the object of their search named as the crucified Nazarene
moves.sitz: the messenger anchors the announcement in the specific dead man whose body they came to tend
moves.paradigm: identification of the addressed dead by name, origin, and manner of death
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the young man

moves.label: M14
moves.paraphrase: He announces that the one they seek has been raised.
moves.substrate: Jesus (as the one whose state is proclaimed)
moves.outcome: the raising declared as accomplished; doer of the raising unnamed
moves.sitz: AD 70 hearers know 'has risen' as a claim that would ordinarily require witnesses; here the claim is delivered BEFORE any witness sees him
moves.paradigm: resurrection-announcement whose agent (God) is left grammatically implicit
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the young man's proclamation

moves.label: M15
moves.paraphrase: He denies that he is present in the tomb.
moves.outcome: not-stated
moves.sitz: the messenger removes the very body the women came to anoint from the frame of the tomb
moves.paradigm: apophatic locative — the absence itself is the evidence
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the young man's negation

moves.label: M16
moves.paraphrase: He directs their attention to the spot where the body had been laid.
moves.operation: direct-attention (behold the place where they laid him)
moves.outcome: the women's gaze turned to the vacated place as evidence
moves.sitz: the messenger anchors the announcement in a physical, checkable spot inside the tomb
moves.paradigm: empty-place ostension — the vacancy is offered as attestation
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the young man

moves.label: M17
moves.paraphrase: The messenger orders the women to depart.
moves.substrate: the women (as those to be dispatched)
moves.outcome: an imperative to leave the tomb on an errand
moves.sitz: messenger dispatching the only present witnesses onward with news
moves.paradigm: commissioning of witnesses at a numinous site
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the young man

moves.label: M18
moves.paraphrase: He orders them to carry word to his followers, singling out Peter.
moves.substrate: M10a (the message they are to convey)
moves.outcome: the women charged to relay the message to the disciples and Peter
moves.sitz: explicit inclusion of Peter marks him despite his prior denial as still addressed
moves.paradigm: chain-of-witness commissioning; the empty tomb becomes news only through relay
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the young man

moves.label: M19
moves.paraphrase: The message promises Jesus is going ahead of them to Galilee.
moves.outcome: Jesus already en route to Galilee ahead of them
moves.sitz: Galilee named as the reunion-site, not Jerusalem
moves.paradigm: shepherd-going-before-flock; reunion relocated to the home country
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the message the young man dictates

moves.label: M20
moves.paraphrase: The message promises they will see him there.
moves.substrate: Jesus (as the one to be seen)
moves.outcome: an encounter foretold in Galilee
moves.sitz: the announcement defers the risen-appearance from the tomb-site to Galilee
moves.paradigm: future-tense witness-promise, not present-tense manifestation
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the message

moves.label: M21
moves.paraphrase: The message anchors itself in Jesus' prior speech to them.
moves.operation: recall prior saying (as he said to you)
moves.outcome: the present promise warranted by Jesus' earlier words
moves.sitz: the messenger presents the Galilee-appearance as fulfillment of something Jesus had already promised
moves.paradigm: warrant-by-prior-word; new event legitimized by earlier prediction
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the young man's citation of Jesus

moves.label: M22
moves.paraphrase: The women rushed out of the tomb in flight.
moves.outcome: the women away from the tomb
moves.sitz: reaction of the just-commissioned witnesses, in the grip of shaking and shock
moves.paradigm: flight from a numinous encounter
moves.narrator: third-person teller reporting the women's departure

moves.label: M23
moves.paraphrase: They kept silent, telling no one anything.
moves.substrate: the message they had just been given (M10a-c)
moves.outcome: the commission un-executed; the news withheld
moves.sitz: the AD 70 hearer, who KNOWS the resurrection was somehow proclaimed, meets the paradox that the first commissioned witnesses said nothing
moves.paradigm: failed-commission / suppressed announcement
moves.narrator: third-person teller reporting the women's non-speech

moves.label: M24
moves.paraphrase: He had been raised early on the week's first day.
moves.operation: rise (early on the first day of the week)
moves.agent: Jesus (as the one risen; the raiser unnamed)
moves.outcome: Jesus alive at daybreak of the first day
moves.sitz: later scribal summary re-narrating the raising as background before the appearance-list
moves.paradigm: resurrection-as-accomplished-event, without depicted raising
moves.narrator: third-person teller (a later editorial voice; the pericope shifts register here)

moves.label: M25
moves.paraphrase: He showed himself first to Mary Magdalene, previously freed by him of seven demons.
moves.substrate: Mary Magdalene (as recipient of the appearance)
moves.outcome: Mary Magdalene as the first to see him alive
moves.sitz: later teller ranks Mary Magdalene as first witness — priority is asserted
moves.paradigm: appearance-list; the risen one initiates contact with a named recipient
moves.narrator: third-person teller listing appearances

moves.label: M26
moves.paraphrase: She set out to those who had been Jesus' companions.
moves.operation: go (to those who had been with him)
moves.substrate: the former companions of Jesus (as those approached)
moves.outcome: Mary arriving among the disciples
moves.sitz: unlike the women in v.8, Mary executes the errand
moves.paradigm: witness-relay initiated by the first appearance-recipient
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M27
moves.paraphrase: She reported to them what had happened.
moves.substrate: the appearance she had received (M14, opaque in the text)
moves.outcome: the disciples informed by her testimony
moves.sitz: first attested resurrection-testimony delivered by a woman to the male disciples
moves.paradigm: witness-relay; the appearance is now propagated by report
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M28
moves.paraphrase: They took in the news that he was alive and that she had seen him.
moves.operation: hear (that he was alive and had been seen by her)
moves.outcome: the report received by them
moves.sitz: the message reaches its recipients, testing whether relay = belief
moves.paradigm: reception-of-testimony as a distinct step from reception-of-truth
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M29
moves.paraphrase: The reported content: he is alive.
moves.outcome: not-stated
moves.sitz: the core proposition the AD 70 hearer is asked to receive
moves.paradigm: resurrection-as-present-state, predicated of the dead one
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the content of Mary's report as heard

moves.label: M30
moves.paraphrase: And: he had been seen by her.
moves.outcome: Mary's eyewitness status established in the report
moves.sitz: eyewitness credential offered as warrant for the state-claim in M17a
moves.paradigm: seeing-by-a-named-witness as evidentiary basis
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the report's second clause

moves.label: M31
moves.paraphrase: They refused to credit it.
moves.outcome: the testimony rejected
moves.sitz: AD 70 teller flags the disciples' initial disbelief as a pattern, not an anomaly
moves.paradigm: testimony-rejection; hearing does not yet compel belief
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M32
moves.paraphrase: Later he showed himself in a different guise to two of them as they were walking out to the countryside.
moves.operation: appear (in another form, to two of them)
moves.outcome: a second appearance, in altered form, to two named-by-role recipients
moves.sitz: later teller catalogs multiple appearances, marking altered-form as a feature
moves.paradigm: appearance-list; risen-Jesus recognizable yet other
moves.narrator: third-person teller continuing the appearance-list

moves.label: M33
moves.paraphrase: The two set off back to the others.
moves.substrate: the rest of the group (as those approached)
moves.outcome: the two arriving back among the others
moves.sitz: second witness-relay attempt, parallel to Mary's
moves.paradigm: witness-relay initiated by appearance-recipients
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M34
moves.paraphrase: They reported what had happened to the others.
moves.outcome: the rest informed by their testimony
moves.sitz: second witness-relay to the wider group
moves.paradigm: propagation of an appearance-report
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M35
moves.paraphrase: The rest again refused to credit them.
moves.outcome: the second testimony also rejected
moves.sitz: the teller drives home a repeated pattern of disbelief across independent witnesses
moves.paradigm: testimony-rejection as a recurring baseline in the resurrection-report chain
moves.narrator: third-person teller marking the pattern as repeated

moves.label: M36
moves.paraphrase: Later he showed himself to the eleven while they were reclining at a meal.
moves.substrate: the eleven (as recipients of the appearance)
moves.outcome: the whole remaining core-group as first-hand recipients at last
moves.sitz: AD 70 teller resolves the failed-relay pattern by having Jesus appear directly to the whole eleven
moves.paradigm: table-appearance to the whole apostolic group
moves.narrator: third-person teller closing the appearance-list with the full group

moves.label: M37
moves.paraphrase: He reproached them for refusing to trust the earlier witnesses and for their obdurate hearts.
moves.operation: rebuke (them for their unbelief and hardness of heart)
moves.substrate: the eleven's unbelief (M18, M22) and hardness of heart
moves.outcome: their prior disbelief named and censured
moves.sitz: the teller stages a formal reckoning with the disbelief pattern he has just narrated
moves.paradigm: rebuke of hardened hearts by the risen one himself
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M38
moves.paraphrase: He addressed them with a commissioning speech.
moves.outcome: the commission and its accompanying promises delivered
moves.sitz: AD 70 teller places the universal-mission mandate in the risen one's own mouth
moves.paradigm: post-resurrection dominical commission
moves.narrator: third-person teller framing the risen one's speech

moves.label: M39
moves.paraphrase: He orders them to travel throughout the whole world.
moves.outcome: the eleven charged with a worldwide errand
moves.sitz: an outward commission to 'all the world' is imaginable to an AD 70 teller writing after the Pauline mission has already gone across the empire
moves.paradigm: sending-out beyond the ethnic boundary
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the commission

moves.label: M40
moves.paraphrase: He orders them to proclaim the good news to every creature.
moves.operation: command (preach the good news to the whole creation)
moves.substrate: the whole creation (as the audience of proclamation)
moves.outcome: the eleven charged with universal proclamation
moves.sitz: 'good news to the whole creation' as an emerging phrase for the post-Jewish-war mission horizon
moves.paradigm: universal proclamation, addressed beyond the human circle
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the commission

moves.label: M41
moves.paraphrase: He promises that whoever trusts the proclamation and is initiated by washing will be delivered.
moves.agent: the risen Jesus (as promiser); God (as implicit saver)
moves.outcome: salvation for the believer-and-baptized
moves.sitz: AD 70 community already practicing baptismal initiation gates salvation-claim by that rite
moves.paradigm: conditional salvation-formula riding on belief plus initiation-rite
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the promise

moves.label: M42
moves.paraphrase: He warns that whoever refuses to trust will be sentenced against.
moves.agent: the risen Jesus (as warner); God (as implicit judge)
moves.outcome: condemnation for the disbeliever
moves.sitz: the same community frames disbelief as a stance with judicial consequence
moves.paradigm: binary salvation/condemnation gate, keyed on belief
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the counterpart warning

moves.label: M43
moves.paraphrase: He promises that a set of signs will attend those who trust the proclamation.
moves.outcome: a set of accompanying signs guaranteed to attend them
moves.sitz: post-70 community with charismatic phenomena in circulation catalogues them here
moves.paradigm: sign-attestation of the believing community
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M44
moves.paraphrase: In his name they will expel demons.
moves.outcome: demons expelled under the invoked name of Jesus
moves.sitz: exorcism-in-Jesus'-name already an attested practice in the AD 70 mission field
moves.paradigm: authority-by-invoked-name
moves.narrator: third-person teller quoting the enumerated sign

moves.label: M45
moves.paraphrase: They will speak in new tongues.
moves.outcome: speech in tongues they had not known
moves.sitz: tongues-phenomenon known to Pauline and post-Pauline communities
moves.paradigm: charismatic speech as sign
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M46
moves.paraphrase: They will handle snakes without harm.
moves.outcome: unharmed handling of snakes
moves.sitz: immunity-signs circulating in the tradition (cf. the Paul-on-Malta story-type)
moves.paradigm: protection-sign in dangerous conditions
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M47
moves.paraphrase: Should they swallow anything lethal, it will do them no harm.
moves.agent: any deadly thing they drink (as would-be harmer)
moves.outcome: no harm despite ingestion
moves.sitz: poison-immunity motif in circulation with holy-figure stories
moves.paradigm: protection-sign against ingested harm
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M48
moves.paraphrase: By touching the sick with their hands, they will bring recovery.
moves.operation: lay hands on the sick → they recover
moves.outcome: recovery of the sick
moves.sitz: laying-on-of-hands as an established healing-gesture in the AD 70 community
moves.paradigm: healing-sign by touch
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M49
moves.paraphrase: Once he finished speaking, the Lord was taken up into heaven.
moves.agent: the Lord (as the one taken); God (as implicit taker)
moves.outcome: his presence removed from earth to heaven
moves.sitz: AD 70 teller closes the pericope with an assumption-scene, common to holy-figure exits in Second Temple imagination
moves.paradigm: assumption of the righteous one to heaven
moves.narrator: third-person teller now naming him 'the Lord' — title shift marks the transition

moves.label: M50
moves.paraphrase: He took his seat at God's right hand.
moves.operation: sit down (at the right hand of God)
moves.outcome: the Lord seated in the position of honor next to God
moves.sitz: Ps 110:1-shaped picture already central to AD 70 confession of the risen one's status
moves.paradigm: session-at-the-right-hand; enthronement of the vindicated one
moves.narrator: third-person teller closing with an enthronement-tableau

moves.label: M51
moves.paraphrase: The eleven set out on the errand.
moves.outcome: the eleven dispatched into the mission
moves.sitz: AD 70 teller shows the commission being executed (contrast with M12's failed relay)
moves.paradigm: commissioned witnesses acting on the mandate
moves.narrator: third-person teller closing with the execution of the commission

moves.label: M52
moves.paraphrase: They proclaimed the message in every place.
moves.substrate: the word / good news (implicit, from M25b)
moves.outcome: the message proclaimed across every place
moves.sitz: AD 70 teller registers that the universal-proclamation mandate was in fact carried out
moves.paradigm: witness-relay finally succeeding on a worldwide scale
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M53
moves.paraphrase: The Lord acted alongside them as they went.
moves.outcome: the mission carried out as joint action of Lord and eleven
moves.sitz: AD 70 community understands its mission as accompanied by the risen Lord it just saw enthroned
moves.paradigm: the enthroned Lord present-with the witnesses even after removal
moves.narrator: third-person teller shifting agency to the enthroned Lord

moves.label: M54
moves.paraphrase: He authenticated the message by means of the signs that came with it.
moves.operation: confirm the word (by the accompanying signs)
moves.outcome: the word authenticated by attendant signs
moves.sitz: AD 70 teller cashes in the sign-promises of M25e-j as the warrant of the proclamation
moves.paradigm: sign-attestation of the proclaimed word
moves.narrator: third-person teller

moves.label: M55
moves.paraphrase: The teller closes with an affirming benediction.
moves.outcome: not-stated
moves.sitz: AD 70 liturgical/scribal closing signature over a completed account
moves.paradigm: amen-formula as ratification, not narrated action
moves.narrator: third-person teller stepping forward to close the pericope in his own voice
